pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
src/index.js defaults view to open, WHERE done=0 ORDER BY id; 'AC-2' test covers / and ?view=open.
'AC-3' test marks 3 and 1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
'AC-4' test expects all three in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is a <strong>, not a link.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400 with no list; 'AC-6' test covers Open, closed, empty and __proto__.
'AC-7' test covers Nothing open, Nothing done yet and No items yet. in all three views of an empty table.
traffic/routes.json lists both views; 'AC-8' test imports it and asserts both are present.

findings.what: The fake app now records the query string, but no traffic test checks that a route with a query is requested with its query. The traffic worker passes the path straight into the URL, so it works today, but nothing guards it.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that a round requests '/?view=done' and sees the query string.

findings.what: The README doesn't say that an unknown view answers 400, or that routes.json entries may now carry a query string.
findings.fix: Add a short note on both.

lenses.note: Spec with go present; the change matches the intent and decisions (open by default, query parameter).
All 8 items and all 6 state rows have named tests. The spec was added in the same change and was not edited after the go.
I could not run npm test because vitest is not installed in the sandbox. I judged the tests by reading them, and they assert behaviour. The traffic test change loosens nothing.
The README mentions the views; the 400 behaviour and query routes are not documented (low).
Queries are static and use no user input in SQL. The hasOwn check blocks prototype keys, and titles are escaped.
The view value is whitelisted, titles are HTML-escaped and no secrets are involved. The traffic route regex now allows '?' but still refuses whitespace and '#'.
The page is a server-rendered unstyled HTML list with no design-system or UI component files in the diff.
There is no browser in this environment, and the PR has no preview or screenshots.
The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim holds, since the spec is unchanged after its creation.
